# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a three-row mapping: blue light requires the red wire, green requires the green wire, and yellow requires the blue wire. I will signal the entries in the manual’s row order, using one, two, and three fingers as ordinal markers for the three wire-color columns.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "✌", "✌", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can feel the button's raised label: PUSH TO DEFUSE. I cannot detect any wire properties or other tactile markings. Please consult the manual and tell me whether to push it or cut a wire.
Deaf says to Mute: Visual bomb state: display reads 0. Indicator light is yellow. There is a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.

The yellow indicator maps to the blue wire. The blue wire is wire 2, and the manual explicitly says the printed button label is bait, so Blind must cut wire 2 rather than push the button. I will signal Deaf with the established ordinal convention: third light-row entry, second wire-color entry.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, yellow indicator, and wires: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. What does the manual require?

Yellow maps to blue, and blue is wire 2. The printed “PUSH TO DEFUSE” label must be ignored; Blind needs the instruction relayed through Deaf, since Blind cannot see my gestures and I cannot speak.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see your gestures, and their meanings are not established. Please communicate the manual's instruction to Deaf in a way Deaf can describe verbally to me next turn.
Deaf says to Mute: Please use gestures to identify the manual rule and required action. First signal the relevant control: 🤟=button, ✌=wire, 👍=display, 👎=light. Then signal the required operation or wire number.

The relevant control is the light, and the yellow light requires cutting wire 2 (the blue wire). Deaf has defined 👎 as the light control and can relay the wire number verbally to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use exactly one gesture to report the manual's required action: thumbs-up means PUSH; index-up means CUT wire 1; V means CUT wire 2; I-love-you means CUT wire 3. Choose the one required for display 0, yellow light, and wires red-blue-green. Do not send two gestures.

Yellow requires the blue wire, and the wires are ordered red, blue, green, so the required action is to cut wire 2. The established gesture for that action is the V sign, and I will send exactly one gesture for Deaf to report verbally to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 6

Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not use an unrequested code. Use exactly this confirmed format: for PUSH, signal 👍 alone; for CUT, signal 👎 followed by the wire number gesture: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. Your reported 👎 then ✌ would mean CUT wire 2. Repeat 👎 then ✌ only if the manual explicitly requires cutting wire 2; otherwise signal the correct format.

The yellow light maps to the blue wire, which is wire 2 in the red-blue-green order. The manual therefore explicitly requires cutting wire 2, so I will use the confirmed format: 👎 followed by ✌.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No action yet. Send exactly one complete code and nothing else: 👍 means PUSH; 👎 then ☝ means CUT wire 1; 👎 then ✌ means CUT wire 2; 👎 then 🤟 means CUT wire 3. Do not send a wire gesture by itself.

The yellow light requires the blue wire, which is wire 2. Using the confirmed complete code, I will signal CUT wire 2.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌"])
```
